$comment: THE SQLITE HARNESS LEG CATALOGUE — the declared, HOST-FREE answer to 'which targets does this harness build?'. D-HARNESS-CROSS-HOST-ANY-TARGET item (2). ★ THE RULE THIS FILE EXISTS TO ENFORCE: the set of legs is a property of the HARNESS, not of the machine running it. Read this file on Windows, on Linux, on an arm64 VPS or on a Mac and you get the SAME five legs. What the host changes is ONLY whether it can EXECUTE a leg's artifact — a separate question, answered by `runOn` + `launchers` below and never by an `if host == ...` in a driver. Before this file existed, build-and-test.sh derived its leg list from `uname` (pe64 was unreachable from any host, macho only from a Mac) and build-and-test.ps1 refused to start unless $IsWindows (pe64 was its ONLY leg, hardcoded). Each driver therefore conflated HOST with TARGET, which is the opposite of the user's hard requirement: 'build ANY target inside ANY host, this MUST work.'
$vocabularyComment: The declaration vocabulary is the CORPUS's, not a new one: `spec` and `runOn` mean exactly what they mean in examples/**/expected.json, and the verdicts a driver records for a leg come from the closed 7+1-name set in tests/test_support/arm_verdict_ledger.hpp (pinned by tests/harness/test_sqlite_harness_legs.cpp, which compares this catalogue's resolver output against that C++ enum). `launchers` is the ONE strict extension: the corpus's `emulator` key covers a cross-ARCH host on the SAME OS, and this harness additionally needs the cross-OS case (a pe64 artifact under Wine on Linux), so both are expressed as one ordered list of declared launchers keyed by (hostOs, hostArch). Absence of a matching launcher entry IS the 'none declared' declaration — there is no empty-string spelling, so a reader cannot mistake 'we looked and there is none' for 'nobody filled this in'. ★ EVERY launcher entry additionally declares `pathTranslation`: the PATH NAMESPACE its argv lives in, from the closed set in harness_legs.py (`none`, `windows-to-wsl`). It is required on every entry, never defaulted, for the same reason `zconfGuards` is: a reader must not have to know a default, and `none` — 'this launcher takes the driver's paths verbatim' — is a CLAIM about the launcher, not an absence. It exists because a launcher need not share a filesystem namespace with the driver that spawns it: `wine /home/me/x.exe` takes the driver's own path, `wsl.exe` needs `/mnt/c/...` where the driver holds a drive-letter path, and an untranslated path does not fail as a path error — the callee opens a relative file by that name, misses, and the run reads as a broken binary. The verb is resolved and APPLIED by harness_legs.py (`--translate-path` / `--assert-translated`), so the translator is named in one file and not in two drivers. ★★ AND `envTransfer`, THE SECOND HALF OF THE SAME FACT, found by measuring the first: a launcher in another OS namespace does not inherit the driver's ENVIRONMENT either. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-04 — a `wsl.exe`-launched fixture saw `SQLITE_TEST_PATTERN_LIST` and `QUICKTEST_OMIT` as EMPTY, so the corpus RESUME ENGINE (which selects its files through that variable) silently re-ran the corpus from the beginning instead of from the abort point: a harness that looks like it is working and is not. `inherit` = the child gets this driver's environment block (qemu, Wine, `arch`); `wslenv` = each variable must be NAMED in the `WSLENV` carrier. Resolved by harness_legs.py (`--env-transfer`), so the carrier and its separator are spelled once.
$noHostKeyingComment: NOTHING in this file may be keyed on the host. `build.libraries.searchPaths` is the one place host-shaped STRINGS appear, and they are CANDIDATES, not decisions: every path is tried on every host, a hit is used and a miss costs nothing. A driver that skips a search path because of the host it is on has reintroduced the defect. ⚠ If you are tempted to add a `"onlyOnHost"` key here, stop: the question you are answering is either 'can this host EXECUTE it' (that is `runOn`/`launchers`) or 'is a declared build input present' (that is a filesystem probe whose failure is the LOUD `skipped-build-input-missing` verdict) — never 'is this leg allowed to exist'.
$configureAnswersComment: ★★ AND THE SAME STORY ONE LAYER UP, FOR SQLITE'S OWN `./configure` (D-HARNESS-MACHO-LEG-INHERITS-THE-DERIVING-LINUX-HOSTS-CONFIGURE-PROBES). The recipe is derived by running `make -n` on the DERIVING host, and the ONE host-probe define left on that command line is `_HAVE_SQLITE_CONFIG_H` — which makes `sqliteInt.h` `#include "sqlite_cfg.h"`, and the include path points at the deriving host's build dir. So EVERY leg inherited THAT machine's ~52 configure answers wholesale. ✔MEASURED, the whole chain, on the macho64-arm64 CLI: the Linux `sqlite_cfg.h` sets `HAVE_PREAD64`/`HAVE_PWRITE64` → `os_unix.c` `#if defined(HAVE_PREAD64) && defined(HAVE_PWRITE64)` → `USE_PREAD64` → the `osPread64`/`osPwrite64` macros, typed with **`off64_t`** — a type Darwin does not have. `off64_t` + `pread64` + `pwrite64` are ONE defect, not three. ⛔ There is NO `HAVE_OFF64_T` macro anywhere in sqlite; the pe64 leg's `$recipeTransformComment` used to name one, and it never existed — that prose is corrected below. ★ THE CLASS IS CLOSED BY MACHINE DIFF, not by reasoning about the header: the deriving Linux `sqlite_cfg.h` against the Mac's OWN configure-generated one differ on EXACTLY THREE LINES — `HAVE_PREAD64`, `HAVE_PWRITE64`, `HAVE_MALLOC_H` — and all ~49 other answers (`HAVE_FDATASYNC`, `HAVE_GMTIME_R`, `HAVE_LOCALTIME_R`, `HAVE_USLEEP`, `HAVE_UTIME`, `HAVE_ISNAN`, `HAVE_NANOSLEEP`, `HAVE_REALPATH`, `HAVE_DLOPEN`, `HAVE_ZLIB`, the `HAVE_INT*_T` family, `SIZEOF_OFF_T 8`, …) are BYTE-IDENTICAL. That is why each leg declares THREE answers and not fifty: it declares only what `configure` actually VARIES across the targets this harness builds, and the deriving host answers the rest — correctly, because on those rows the two machines agree. Each leg's `build.configureAnswers` is REQUIRED, its values are real JSON booleans, and harness_legs.py's lint CROSS-CHECKS every one against the leg's own target (a Darwin leg declaring `HAVE_PREAD64: true` is refused, naming the evidence), so a wrong declaration fails the lint instead of shipping. The drivers then stage ONE `sqlite_cfg.h` per TARGET OS — the deriving host's answers for the identical rows, the leg's declared answers for the three that vary — into the harness's OWN cfg/ dir, placed AHEAD of the deriving host's build dir on the include list. `_HAVE_SQLITE_CONFIG_H` STAYS. ⚠ NOTE THE KEY IS THE TARGET OS AND NOT THE `recipeTransform`: four legs share `"none"` and they are TWO configurations (two Linux, two Darwin), so keying this on the transform would hand Darwin the Linux answers again — which is the defect. ⛔ TWO ALTERNATIVES WERE REJECTED, recorded because both are the obvious thing to reach for. (1) DERIVE THE RECIPE PER TARGET, on a machine of that target: that is what upstream's build system expects and it is why a native build never has this bug, but it makes the Darwin legs unbuildable on the four hosts out of five that are not a Mac — flatly the host-lock this file exists to end. (2) A BLUNT `darwin-selfconfig` TRANSFORM that just drops `_HAVE_SQLITE_CONFIG_H`, mirroring `windows-selfconfig`: ✔MEASURED to WORK, and still wrong — it discards ~49 CORRECT answers to fix 3 wrong ones, ~10 of them with real consequences (`HAVE_GMTIME_R`/`HAVE_LOCALTIME_R` fall back to the NON-REENTRANT `gmtime`/`localtime` in a SQLITE_THREADSAFE=1 build; `HAVE_FDATASYNC` becomes `#define fdatasync fsync`; `HAVE_USLEEP` drops sqlite3_sleep to 1-SECOND granularity, which the timing-sensitive corpus WILL notice). The same blunt drop is acceptable on WINDOWS only because `SQLITE_OS_WIN` re-configures the whole `os_win.c` path and none of those Unix answers is consulted there.
$stagedHeadersComment: ★ THE THIRD-PARTY HEADERS A LEG COMPILES AGAINST ARE A TARGET FACT, NOT A HOST ONE (D-HARNESS-SQLITE-STAGE-ZCONF-IS-PE-SHAPED, closed TF-C115). The staged zlib header is copied from the DERIVING POSIX host, where `./configure` baked ITS OWN probe results into zconf.h — `#if 1 → #define Z_HAVE_UNISTD_H` and friends. Those are facts about the deriving machine, exactly like the recipe's HAVE_*/Z_HAVE_* defines that `recipeTransform` exists to drop, and handing them to a foreign target is the same cross-compile category error one level down. Each leg therefore DECLARES `build.zconfGuards` — the value ITS target has for each guard `./configure` may have set — and the drivers stage ONE zinc/ PER `recipeTransform` (stage-zinc.py, called by both) and give each leg an include list pointing at its own. Two legs may share a zinc/ only by sharing a recipeTransform, and the lint refuses a catalogue where same-transform legs declare different guards. Before this, ONE pe-shaped zinc/ served every leg and the .ps1 REFUSED (`poisoned`) any leg that was not `windows-selfconfig` rather than compile it against the wrong header — the right call, and the reason this key exists is to make the refusal unnecessary instead of relaxing it.
$loadExtHelperBuilderComment: ★★★ THE COMPILER THIS REPOSITORY SHIPS BUILDS THE CORPUS'S dlopen()ed HELPER — NO HOST NEEDS A THIRD-PARTY CROSS-COMPILER FOR ANY LEG. Operator, 2026-08-05: 'why do we need mingw? since dss code prime should not have dependencies?' / 'I installed mingw in wsl, but we should NOT depend on a tool'. The `$targetCcComment` below is still TRUE and its rule is unchanged — a compiler's name is not a declaration of its target — but the SHAPE it left behind made every leg's RUN conditional on this machine owning a cross-compiler for that leg's target (a mingw gcc for pe64, aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc for the arm64 leg, an Apple clang for the two macho legs), and a leg without one recorded `skipped-build-input-missing` and did not run its ~330,000 units. That is the same host-lock D-HARNESS-CROSS-HOST-ANY-TARGET exists to end, one layer down from the fixture. ⇒ each leg now DECLARES `build.sharedLibFormat` and DSS emits the helper for it. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-05 on this project's WINDOWS box — one host, all five legs, rc=0 and zero diagnostics on every one: pe64 8,704 B · elf64-x86_64 13,912 B · elf64-aarch64 13,912 B · macho64-arm64 67,426 B · macho64-x86_64 17,890 B. The three a machine here can LOAD were loaded THROUGH SQLITE'S OWN `sqlite3_load_extension()` (dlopen + dlsym `testloadext_init`, exactly what test/loadext.test does) and `SELECT half(9.0)` returned 4.500 — pe64 natively on Windows, elf64-x86_64 in WSL, elf64-aarch64 under qemu-aarch64; the loading program was built by the REFERENCE compiler each time, so the only thing under test was the DSS artefact. ★ THE CONTROL IS KEPT, DELIBERATELY, BECAUSE DSS IS NOW TESTING DSS: a defect SHARED by the fixture and the helper (both compile sqlite3ext.h) could cancel and read as green. So wherever a VERIFIED target compiler happens to exist, the same source is ALSO built with it and both artefacts are reported side by side — never gating, never staging — and `DSS_LOADEXT_HELPER=reference` STAGES the control instead, which makes the corpus itself the differential. There is NO automatic fallback: a DSS emission failure is a compiler defect and this harness exists to surface them, so it is `poisoned` with the diagnostics quoted, never quietly rebuilt another way.
$targetCcComment: ★★ A COMPILER'S NAME IS NOT A DECLARATION OF ITS TARGET, and this catalogue once said it was. ⚠ READ `$loadExtHelperBuilderComment` FIRST: since 2026-08-05 this key governs the optional CONTROL arm, not a required build input — a leg whose `targetCc` resolves to nothing on this host still builds its helper (with DSS) and still runs its corpus. D-HARNESS-LOADEXT-HELPER-TARGET-BLINDNESS-NOW-ABORTS-THE-RUN. `build.targetCc.candidates` is a list of names to TRY, in order; it is NOT a list of compilers that are known to build this leg. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-05 on a WSL/Ubuntu x86_64 host: both elf legs ran GREEN (6 err / 331,351 and 5 err / 331,355, all known confounds) and the run then DIED in /usr/bin/ld — 'relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against symbol `sqlite3_api` can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC' — building the pe64 leg's loadext helper, and pe64's units never ran. The mingw cross-compiler was absent, this leg listed plain `gcc` as an ALTERNATIVE, and so a LINUX compiler was picked, legitimately, to build a WINDOWS shared object. build-and-test.sh:2615 and :3804 both forbid exactly that fallback in so many words; neither guard fired, because the config had already licensed what the guards were watching for. ⇒ THE RESOLVER NOW ASKS THE COMPILER. harness_legs.py `--resolve-target-cc <leg>` accepts a candidate only if `<cc> -dumpmachine` names this leg's own target arch AND target OS, both derived from the leg's declared `spec`. No new key, because the leg already declares its target; no host test; no format-name branch. A candidate that CANNOT state its target (the probe fails) is REFUSED, never assumed — the leg is still BUILT, it records `skipped-build-input-missing`, and its corpus does not run. ★ AND THE RULE IS NOT pe64-SHAPED: the elf64-x86_64 leg's `cc`/`gcc`/`clang` resolve to an aarch64 compiler on this project's native arm64 Linux VPS, which is the wrong-arch helper D-HARNESS-ARM64-LEG-HOST-ARCH-HELPER-SO is named after; the same one check refuses it. ★★ WHAT IT BUILDS is the corpus's dlopen()ed helper extension, whose FILE NAME is also a target fact — see each leg's `loadExtHelperName`.

legs.label: elf64-x86_64
legs.$launchersComment: qemu-x86_64 lets an arm64 Linux host run this leg. ★ NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH THE CORPUS, which is a finding and not a copy error: examples/**/expected.json declares NO emulator on its (x86_64, linux) arms, so on the native arm64 Linux VPS every one of them is a structural skip even though qemu-x86_64 exists. This catalogue declares it; the corpus's omission is tracked separately (D-TEST-CORPUS-NO-QEMU-X86_64-ON-ARM64-HOST). ★★ `wsl.exe` IS THE SECOND ENTRY AND IT CLOSES D-HARNESS-NO-WSL-LAUNCHER-FOR-ELF-ON-WINDOWS. A Windows host BUILDS this leg (TF-C115 did) and could always have RUN it — the artefact built by build-and-test.ps1 passed 330,436 tests under WSL BY HAND — but nothing declared the launcher, so the driver recorded `skipped-by-runOn` beside a binary it had just produced. It is not a plain command entry: wsl.exe lives in a DIFFERENT PATH NAMESPACE from the driver that spawns it (`pathTranslation`) AND in a different ENVIRONMENT namespace (`envTransfer`). The second was found by measuring the first — with paths translated but the environment assumed to inherit, the corpus resume engine's file selection arrived EMPTY and the resume re-ran the whole corpus while looking like it worked. ★★★ AND THE THIRD NAMESPACE, WHICH IS THE ARGV ITSELF: the command is `wsl.exe -e`, and this entry said `wsl.exe --` until 2026-08-04. `--` is documented as 'pass the remaining command line as is' and it is NOT the same as `-e`/`--exec` — ✔MEASURED on this host, one variable changed: `wsl.exe -- /nope` answers `/bin/bash: line 1: /nope: No such file` while `wsl.exe -e /nope` answers `execvpe(/nope) failed`, i.e. `--` reconstructs a command LINE and feeds it to the distro's DEFAULT SHELL. That shell then expands the fixture's argv a second time — MEASURED, a single argument `/mnt/c/.../g/*.test` came back to the callee as TWO arguments under `--` and as one under `-e`, and `$`, backticks, `;` and the backslash escape are live there too. A launcher whose argv is silently re-parsed cannot be trusted to have run the file the driver named, which is the same class of defect as an untranslated path. Recorded as D-TOOLS-WSL-EXE-WITHOUT-DASH-E-RUNS-A-LOCAL-SHELL and pinned by tests/harness/test_sqlite_harness_legs.cpp.

build.$zconfGuardsComment: See the pe64 leg for the whole story. This target HAS <unistd.h>, so zlib must see it — which is what the deriving Linux host's ./configure already decided, so these values are the staged header's own.
build.$configureAnswersComment: See the top-level $configureAnswersComment. THIS leg is the DERIVING host's own target, so these three are exactly what its `./configure` wrote and the staged header is byte-identical to the one it generated — which is the point of staging it anyway rather than special-casing 'the deriving host's leg needs no stage': that special case is a HOST fact, and it would be wrong the moment the harness is driven from a Mac.
build.$sharedLibFormatComment: ★ THE OBJECT FORMAT DSS EMITS THIS LEG'S loadext HELPER IN — see the top-level $loadExtHelperBuilderComment. It is DECLARED rather than derived for the same reason `loadExtHelperName` is: this string IS the `--target <arch>:<format>` argument, there is no separate --object-format flag, and the arch and the format spell arm64 DIFFERENTLY (`arm64:elf64-aarch64-linux-dyn` — arch arm64, format aarch64), which has cost this project failed invocations. A reader of this file must be able to SEE the exact argument. It is then cross-checked by harness_legs.py's lint against this leg's own `spec`: same container/arch/OS, kind replaced by the container's shared-library kind (elf64 -> dyn, pe64 -> dll, macho64 -> dylib — ✔MEASURED from the shipped src/dss-config/object-formats/, where each container ships exactly one). `sharedLibFlags` above stays: it is the CONTROL arm's recipe, and a control whose command changed alongside the thing it controls is not a control.
build.$loadExtHelperNameComment: The name sqlite's own test/loadext.test looks for on a `tcl_platform(platform) eq unix` fixture. See the top-level $targetCcComment for why the name is DECLARED per leg instead of spelled once in a driver.
build.$librariesComment: ★ THIS LEG ACQUIRES ITS LIBRARIES TOO, and it is the one whose old provider looked harmless. `host-system` means 'hope this box has an x86_64 Linux libtcl' — true on WSL, FALSE on Windows, on a Mac, and on the arm64 VPS (which has aarch64 libraries, not x86_64 ones), so three of four hosts recorded `skipped-build-input-missing` for the most-tested leg in the harness. That is a BUILD failure, and the build half of D-HARNESS-CROSS-HOST-ANY-TARGET admits no exceptions. ⚠ THE SOURCE IS DEBIAN, NOT UBUNTU, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED (2026-08-06): every Ubuntu .deb — amd64 AND arm64, jammy through current — ships `data.tar.zst`, and zstd entered the Python stdlib only in 3.14 while this project's WSL host runs 3.12, so 'the Ubuntu amd64 archive, literal sibling of the arm64 provider' cannot be opened by a mechanism that must work on every host. The old arm64 provider opened one only because it shelled out to `dpkg-deb`, a tool no Windows or macOS box has — i.e. it was never the portable sibling it looked like. Debian bookworm's are `data.tar.xz`, which `tarfile` opens everywhere. ✔MEASURED: 883 exported symbols, 880 of them `Tcl*`, a SUPERSET of nothing missing against the MacPorts 8.6.17 library this harness already proved 110/110 against (the 11 names MacPorts has and this does not are all `TclMacOSX*`/`TclBN_mp_*`, none of which a Linux fixture references).

libraries.$importNameComment: The identities recorded are the ones the file DECLARES for itself — DT_SONAME `libtcl8.6.so` and `libz.so.1` — i.e. byte-for-byte what the old `host-system` route already recorded when it resolved the host's own copies. They are DECLARED anyway rather than left empty: an acquired library is a stand-in by construction, and 'the packager's identity happens to be right here' is a fact worth stating where a reader can check it, not a default to lean on.

archives.$urlComment: Debian bookworm's pool. ⚠ The pool holds the CURRENT version of a package for a suite, so a point release can retire this file; the digest is pinned, so that failure is a loud 404 or a CHECKSUM MISMATCH and never a silently different library. snapshot.debian.org is the permanent mirror if it ever comes to that.

members.$runtimeCopyComment: The staged directory goes on LD_LIBRARY_PATH for this leg's run, so the copy acquired here is the copy the fixture loads — which is why the script library below is not optional. Before this, the leg happened to work because Debian and Ubuntu spell the script directory the same way (`/usr/share/tcltk/tcl8.6`); that is a coincidence between two distributions, not a property of the target.

embeddedPaths.$why: the PARENT of the script directory, used to build the search list `tclInit` walks. Staging the child is what makes the search succeed; the parent itself holds no file Tcl reads.
Debian's directory for Tcl EXTENSION packages (a second element of `tcl_pkgPath`). The testfixture loads no extension — its commands are compiled in.
the versioned twin of the above, same reason.
the multiarch twin of the above, same reason. Note the TARGET's arch in the name — this is why the two elf legs' declarations differ at all.
the local-admin extension directory in `tcl_pkgPath`; on the target it usually does not exist, and nothing here requires it to.
the local-admin twin of /usr/share/tcltk, same reason.
TCL_EXEC_PREFIX/lib from tclConfig.sh, reported for build consumers.
the multiarch libdir from the same tclConfig.sh block — where the packager's own copy of THIS library sits, not data.
TCL_INCLUDE_SPEC, a BUILD-time answer. This harness stages its own tcl.h and cross-checks its version against this very library.
the manual page directory, from the same block. No interpreter code path reads it.
the default PATH element Tcl's `exec` falls back on — a target path, not shipped data.
`exec`'s redirection sink; a device on the target.
the controlling terminal for interactive prompting; same category as /dev/null.

archives.$memberComment: `lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libz.so.1` is a SYMLINK to `libz.so.1.2.13` inside the .deb; the resolver follows it and materialises the target's bytes under the `as` name, exactly as it does for MacPorts' libz.

members.$embeddedPathsComment: EMPTY, and MEASURED: this .so carries no absolute path at all. zlib reads no data directory, which is what makes it the control for the Tcl declaration above.

legs.label: elf64-arm64
legs.$launchersComment: qemu-aarch64 for a cross-ARCH Linux host, and `wsl.exe` for the cross-OS case — the same pair, one arch over. ⚠ THE wsl.exe ENTRY IS DECLARED AND NOT MEASURED, and it is labelled so rather than omitted: WSL2 runs the HOST's architecture, so an arm64 Windows box runs an arm64 Linux distro and therefore this leg (DOCUMENTED, Microsoft's WSL2-on-ARM64 support; no arm64 Windows machine exists in this project to measure it on). Omitting it would have been the worse error — it would say `wsl.exe only works for x86_64`, which is a claim about the launcher that is FALSE, and a Windows/arm64 host would then record `skipped-by-runOn` for the one Linux target it can actually execute. ★ `-e` (not `--`) for the reason spelled out on the elf64-x86_64 leg: `--` re-parses the fixture's argv in the distro's default shell. That fact is about wsl.exe and not about either arch, so unlike the entry itself it is MEASURED, not merely declared.

build.$configureAnswersComment: Same target OS as the elf64-x86_64 leg, so the SAME three answers and the SAME staged sqlite_cfg.h — the stage key is the TARGET OS, and two legs on one OS share one header (harness_legs.py refuses a catalogue where they disagree). `pread64`/`pwrite64` are glibc LFS64 names, not x86-64 ones: the arm64 glibc exports them too.
build.$sharedLibFormatComment: ★ NOTE THE TWO SPELLINGS OF arm64 IN ONE ARGUMENT — the target arch is `arm64` (from this leg's spec) and the FORMAT says `aarch64`. `--target arm64:elf64-aarch64-linux-dyn` is what harness_legs.py's shared_lib_spec() assembles from the two; neither driver spells it.
build.$targetCcComment: The CONTROL arm only (top-level $loadExtHelperBuilderComment). `package` is still declared so an operator who ASKS for the control (DSS_LOADEXT_HELPER=reference) is told what to install — the drivers no longer install it unasked, because a control must not mutate the machine it runs on.
build.$librariesComment: ★ THE ORIGINAL BESPOKE PROVIDER, RETIRED — D-HARNESS-UBUNTU-PORTS-PROVIDER-NOT-GENERALISED-TO-PINNED-ARCHIVE. This leg used to declare `ubuntu-ports-arm64`, ~80 lines of `curl` + `dpkg-deb` living inside build-and-test.sh and NOWHERE ELSE, so on Windows the leg returned a named refusal (`library provider … has no dispatch arm in build-and-test.ps1`) instead of building. The deferral that kept it was correct at the time and its reasoning still holds: the obvious generalisation needed a zstd reader, which is Python 3.14+, and this project has a 3.12 host — a capability that exists on one HOST and not another is the same defect one level down. What changed is the SOURCE, not the appetite: Debian's .debs are `data.tar.xz`, so the general route opens them with the stdlib on every host, and `dpkg-deb` is not needed at all. The self-retiring exemption in tests/harness/test_sqlite_harness_legs.cpp goes with it. ⓘ The old provider also fetched `libtommath1`; this one does not, because Debian's libtcl8.6 does not link it (✔MEASURED: DT_NEEDED = libz.so.1, libm.so.6, libc.so.6) and the old code itself treated it as optional.

libraries.$importNameComment: See the elf64-x86_64 leg — same rule, same reasoning, and the SAME two names: DT_SONAME is architecture-independent.

archives.$embeddedPathsComment: The SAME fourteen paths as the amd64 sibling with the multiarch triple respelled — ✔MEASURED on both files, and the difference is exactly the two `x86_64-linux-gnu` -> `aarch64-linux-gnu` entries. A declaration that could not tell them apart would be a declaration that was not read from the bytes.

Debian's directory for Tcl EXTENSION packages (a second element of `tcl_pkgPath`). The testfixture loads no extension — its commands are compiled in.
the versioned twin of the above, same reason.
the multiarch twin of the above, same reason. THE TARGET's arch, not the host's — this entry is what an arch-blind copy of the amd64 declaration would have got wrong.
the local-admin extension directory in `tcl_pkgPath`; on the target it usually does not exist, and nothing here requires it to.
the local-admin twin of /usr/share/tcltk, same reason.
TCL_EXEC_PREFIX/lib from tclConfig.sh, reported for build consumers.
the multiarch libdir from the same tclConfig.sh block — where the packager's own copy of THIS library sits, not data.
TCL_INCLUDE_SPEC, a BUILD-time answer. This harness stages its own tcl.h and cross-checks its version against this very library.
the manual page directory, from the same block. No interpreter code path reads it.
the default PATH element Tcl's `exec` falls back on — a target path, not shipped data.
`exec`'s redirection sink; a device on the target.

legs.label: pe64-x86_64
legs.$launchersComment: Wine is the declared cross-OS launcher. It is a DECLARATION, not a claim that it is installed: a host without it records `skipped-emulator-missing` (environmental, loud, promotable to a hard failure) rather than vanishing. No launcher is declared for a non-x86_64 host: Wine alone does not emulate the ISA.

build.$recipeTransformComment: The recipe is derived from a POSIX `make -n`, so any host feature-probe define it carries is a fact about the DERIVING host, never about this target. `windows-selfconfig` drops those and adds SQLITE_OS_WIN=1 so SQLite self-configures its Windows build. ⚠ WHICH DEFINES, PRECISELY — ✔MEASURED 2026-08-05 (TF-C121) against the recipe this harness actually derives: `_HAVE_SQLITE_CONFIG_H` is the ONE such define on the command line. There is NO bare `HAVE_*` and NO `Z_HAVE_*` in `stage/defines.txt` or `stage/cli-defines.txt` at all (the only near-miss is `SQLITE_HAVE_ZLIB=1`, a project feature flag the transform's `^(HAVE_|Z_HAVE_)` regex deliberately does not match). This comment used to list `HAVE_*/Z_HAVE_*` alongside it as if all three families were present; the regex arm is a standing guard against a future recipe, not a description of this one. See `$configureAnswersComment` above, which states the same fact, and gen-pe64-manifest.py's transform block. Keyed on THIS LEG, which is why the rule moved out of gen-pe64-manifest.py's prose ('this generator is pe-only, so keying the rule on the pe target is inherent here') into a declaration any driver can read.
build.$zconfGuardsComment: THE HEADER HALF OF THE SAME CROSS-COMPILE CATEGORY ERROR the recipeTransform fixes, and until TF-C115 the ONLY leg it was applied for — by a `perl -0777 -pi` flip buried in one driver's staging step, against ONE zinc/ shared by every leg, which is why a non-pe leg had to be REFUSED (`poisoned`) rather than built. The staged zconf.h comes from the deriving POSIX host, where ./configure wrote `#if 1 → #define Z_HAVE_UNISTD_H`; that is a fact about THAT HOST, and on a Windows TARGET <unistd.h> does not exist. Each guard is now DECLARED per leg and one zinc/ is staged per recipeTransform (stage-zinc.py), so every leg parses a zlib header configured for ITS OWN target and no leg is refused. ★ Z_HAVE_STDARG_H stays true: <stdarg.h> is C-standard and exists on pe. ★ MEASURED (TF-C115) on the elf64-x86_64 leg, both gcc and DSS: with these recipe defines the ONLY thing the guard changes is `z_off_t` = off_t vs long — the same 8-byte `long` on LP64 — and SEEK_*/z_off64_t/the gz* symbol names are byte-identical either way. So the flip is BENIGN on LP64; it is NOT benign on the pe target, where the guard's `#include <unistd.h>` simply does not resolve.
build.$configureAnswersComment: ★ DECLARED, AND INERT ON THIS LEG — both halves matter. INERT: `windows-selfconfig` drops `_HAVE_SQLITE_CONFIG_H`, so sqliteInt.h never includes ANY sqlite_cfg.h here and no answer below is read. DECLARED ANYWAY: every leg declares every answer so a reader never has to know a default, and — more to the point — these are claims about the TARGET, which stay true whatever a transform does with them. `pread64`/`pwrite64` are glibc LFS64 names that no Windows CRT has. `HAVE_MALLOC_H` is TRUE: ✔MEASURED on this project's Windows box, the UCRT ships `malloc.h` under the Windows SDK's `ucrt/` include dir (`C:/Program Files (x86)/Windows Kits/10/Include/<ver>/ucrt/malloc.h`), so declaring it false would be a false statement about the target that happens to be unread. If this leg ever stops dropping `_HAVE_SQLITE_CONFIG_H`, these are already the right answers and nothing here needs revisiting.
build.$stackReserveComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH — Windows defaults a process to 1 MiB; e_fkey-63.1.x recurses to SQLITE_MAX_TRIGGER_DEPTH and overflows it (a NATIVE gcc build overflows too). 8 MiB = what Linux hands the process for free.
build.$sharedLibFormatComment: ★ THE LEG THAT MADE THE CASE. Until 2026-08-05 running this leg REQUIRED a mingw cross-compiler on the host — `x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc`, or a `gcc` that reports `x86_64-w64-mingw32` — and on a Linux/WSL box without one its whole corpus was skipped. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-05: DSS emits this format from a Windows host in well under a second (8,704 bytes), the artefact is a real PE with IMAGE_FILE_DLL set and exports `testloadext_init`/`testbrokenext_init`/`sqlite3_api`, and sqlite's own `sqlite3_load_extension()` loaded it and answered `SELECT half(9.0)` = 4.500.
build.$loadExtHelperNameComment: ★ THE ONE LEG WHOSE NAME IS DIFFERENT, and the reason this key exists. ✔MEASURED from the staged upstream tree, test/loadext.test:26-29: a `tcl_platform(platform) eq windows` fixture looks for `./testloadext.dll` — the drivers hardcoded `libtestloadext.so` for every leg, so a pe64 fixture never found the staged helper and fell through to loadext.test's own hardcoded-`gcc` self-build, which is precisely the fallback the pre-staging exists to prevent [D-HARNESS-ARM64-LEG-HOST-ARCH-HELPER-SO].
build.$targetCcComment: `gcc` STAYS on this list and it is not a mistake: ✔MEASURED 2026-08-05 on this project's Windows box, `gcc -dumpmachine` prints `x86_64-w64-mingw32` (Git for Windows and Strawberry both ship mingw gcc under the bare name), so on a Windows host it IS this leg's correct compiler. What was missing is the CHECK, not a shorter list — see the top-level $targetCcComment.
build.$librariesComment: pe64 --resolve-library reads a DLL's EXPORT table (.edata), so these must be real DLLs, not import .libs. A DLL is just a FILE: DSS reads a PE export table on any host, so ANY box that HAS these files can build this leg — and the old `search-paths` provider is precisely the reason no non-Windows box had them. ✔MEASURED: the leg was `skipped-build-input-missing` on the arm64 VPS and on macOS, because every declared search path was a Windows install location plus a cache nothing ever populated. Searching for a file the machine was never given is not acquisition. ⚠ THE OBVIOUS SOURCE IS BLOCKED, MEASURED 2026-08-06: msys2/mingw64 — the repo D-HARNESS-LIBRARY-ACQUISITION-BUILT-FOR-ONE-LEG-IN-ONE-DRIVER names, and the source of the very `tcl86.dll` Git for Windows ships — publishes `.pkg.tar.zst` and NOTHING ELSE (every tcl and zlib package, checked directly). zstd entered the Python stdlib in 3.14 and this project has a 3.12 host, so that route would be a capability that exists on one host and not another. conda-forge's win-64 packages are plain `.tar.bz2`, unauthenticated HTTPS, content-addressable, and carry the SCRIPT LIBRARY as well — so the pe64 leg becomes self-contained instead of borrowing from an installed Git.

libraries.$importNameComment: Bare DLL names, and on Windows that IS the beside-the-artefact spelling: the loader searches the application's own directory FIRST, so a DLL staged next to the executable wins with no path recorded and no assumption about the target's layout — the same argument `@loader_path` makes on Darwin, spelled the way this loader spells it. Each DLL's own PE export-directory Name already agrees (`tcl86t.dll`, `zlib.dll`), so nothing is being displaced here; it is declared because 'the packager's identity happens to be right' is a fact a reader should be able to check.
libraries.$tclNamesComment: `tcl86t.dll` is conda-forge's THREADED build — the `t` suffix is the Windows convention for `--enable-threads`, which is also how msys2 and ActiveState ship it, and what sqlite's testfixture wants. The older unsuffixed names stay in the list: they are what a `search-paths` era cache or a Git-for-Windows install still holds, and this list is matched against whatever is staged.

archives.$archiveComment: conda-forge's `tk` package carries BOTH tcl86t.dll and tk86t.dll plus the whole `Library/lib/tcl8.6` script tree (830 files, ✔MEASURED, including init.tcl and Tcl's own tzdata). There is no separate `tcl` package for win-64 — Tcl ships inside `tk` — which is why the archive's name does not say Tcl.

members.$embeddedPathsComment: ★ THE GUARD EARNED ITS KEEP HERE. A first pass with a POSIX-only path scan reported ZERO embedded paths in this DLL and concluded Windows Tcl locates its scripts purely relative to the module — the resolver's own scanner, which understands `X:\`, found FIVE, and one of them is the script library under conda's BUILD prefix on a machine that no longer exists. Had the scan been the naive one, this leg would have shipped a Tcl that hunts `D:\bld\…` for init.tcl and dies at `interp create`, which is exactly the failure the anchor is named after — found here by the guard rather than by a Mac.

embeddedPaths.$why: the build prefix's libdir, baked in as `tcl_pkgPath` for an extension search the testfixture never performs. It names a directory on conda-forge's build machine and cannot resolve anywhere else — which is harmless only because nothing reads it.
the build prefix's bindir, from the same baked-in configuration block.
the build prefix's include dir — a BUILD-time answer for tclConfig consumers. This harness stages its own tcl.h.
the build prefix's doc dir, from the same block. No interpreter code path reads it.

archives.$archiveComment: conda-forge splits zlib's runtime DLL into `libzlib`; the `zlib` package is the development half. The DLL is at `Library/bin/zlib.dll` and the archive also carries a top-level copy — the declaration names the `Library/` one so both members come from the same prefix.

members.$embeddedPathsComment: EMPTY, and MEASURED with the same scanner that found five in tcl86t.dll — so the emptiness is a result, not an omission.

libraries.$searchPathsComment: EMPTIED with the provider change, deliberately. A candidate list nothing consults is worse than none: a reader would take it for the mechanism. The escape hatch that replaces `DSS_PE_LIBDIR` is `DSS_HARNESS_CACHE_ROOT` — it moves where the pinned archives are materialised, and unlike a search path it cannot silently substitute a different library, because what lands there is checked against the pinned digest.

legs.label: macho64-arm64
legs.$launchersComment: EMPTY, and the emptiness is the hardest-won fact in this file: there is NO off-Mac emulator for a Darwin arm64 executable. Unlike pe-under-Wine or aarch64-under-qemu, the only way to observe this artifact RUN is a real Mac — which is exactly why TF-C113 proved it by BUILDING it on a Windows host and shipping the binary to one. So this leg's build is attempted everywhere and its run is a structural skip everywhere but Darwin/arm64. Do not invent a launcher here.

build.$recipeTransformComment: ★ `none` IS RIGHT AFTER ALL, AND THE FIX WENT SOMEWHERE ELSE — read `$configureAnswersComment` at the top of this file first. THE HISTORY IS KEPT because the diagnosis in it was correct and only the REMEDY moved: this comment used to say `none` IS WRONG HERE. TF-C117 was the cycle that could finally see the failure (before it, the leg died at Step 6 for want of a Darwin libtcl on a non-Mac), and ✔MEASURED the fixture then failed with 8 diagnostics whose load-bearing ones were `error[S0001] got pread64`, `got pwrite64` and `error[S0006] got off64_t` — LINUX names, inherited from the deriving host. ⛔ ONE THING IT SAID WAS SIMPLY FALSE and is corrected here rather than quietly dropped: it named `HAVE_OFF64_T` as an inherited configure answer. THERE IS NO SUCH MACRO IN SQLITE. `off64_t` arrives through `HAVE_PREAD64` + `HAVE_PWRITE64` → `os_unix.c` `USE_PREAD64` → the `osPread64`/`osPwrite64` macro casts; the three are ONE defect with ONE cause, and a reader hunting for `HAVE_OFF64_T` would find nothing and conclude the chain was unexplained. WHY `none` STAYS: the leak is not on the command line, it is INSIDE a header (`_HAVE_SQLITE_CONFIG_H` → `sqliteInt.h` → `#include "sqlite_cfg.h"`), so a recipe transform is the wrong instrument — the only transform that could reach it is the blunt one that drops `_HAVE_SQLITE_CONFIG_H` wholesale, and that discards ~49 CORRECT answers to fix 3 wrong ones (rejected, with its measured consequences, in `$configureAnswersComment`). The leg instead DECLARES its three answers below and the drivers stage it a Darwin `sqlite_cfg.h`. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-05 on the real 103-TU CLI manifest at `--config=release`, from a WINDOWS host: recipe verbatim → 4 errors (`off64_t`×2, `pread64`, `pwrite64`); with the staged header → ZERO, and a real Mach-O arm64 executable. ★ Without the leak sqlite self-configures Darwin CORRECTLY — `os_unix.c` keys on `__APPLE__`, which DSS already predefines for macho. (The `sysctlbyname`/`CTL_HW`/`HW_AVAILCPU`/`HW_NCPU` diagnostics that used to accompany these were a SEPARATE and genuine gap — a Darwin `<sys/sysctl.h>` descriptor DSS did not ship — and have since been closed.)
build.$configureAnswersComment: ★ THE LEG THAT MADE THE CASE — see the top-level $configureAnswersComment for the whole chain. All three are FALSE on Darwin, and all three are MEASURED on the operator's real Mac (macOS 26.5.2, arm64) TWICE OVER: once as that Mac's OWN `./configure`-generated `sqlite_cfg.h` (`/* #undef HAVE_PREAD64 */`, `/* #undef HAVE_PWRITE64 */`, `/* #undef HAVE_MALLOC_H */`), and once by re-running sqlite's own probe methodology against `/usr/bin/cc` — `pread64`/`pwrite64` LINK-FAIL (plain `pread`/`pwrite` LINK-OK), `malloc.h` HDR-MISS, `off64_t` TYPE-MISS, `off_t` TYPE-OK at 8 bytes. ⚠ `HAVE_MALLOC_H` has never actually fired: `mem1.c` reads `#if HAVE_MALLOC_H && HAVE_MALLOC_USABLE_SIZE`, and `HAVE_MALLOC_USABLE_SIZE` is absent on the deriving host too. It is declared anyway because it is the same leak from the same header, and 'it happens not to fire today' is not a reason to ship an answer that is false about this target.
build.$sharedLibFormatComment: ★ THE FILE NAME AND THE FORMAT DISAGREE ON THIS TARGET, AND BOTH ARE RIGHT. The declared `loadExtHelperName` below is `libtestloadext.so` — sqlite's own choice, MEASURED, see its comment — while the object format is a `dylib`. DSS emits `<stem>.dylib` and the driver STAGES it under the name the corpus looks for; the extension in a Mach-O file's name has never been what makes it loadable. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-05 from a Windows host: 67,426 bytes, `Mach-O 64-bit arm64 dynamically linked shared library, flags:<NOUNDEFS|DYLDLINK|TWOLEVEL|NO_REEXPORTED_DYLIBS>`. ⚠ It has NOT been LOADED — there is no off-Mac loader for it, which is the same structural fact this leg's empty `launchers` list already declares. Emission is measured; loading is not, and is not claimed.
build.$loadExtHelperNameComment: The `.so` spelling, on a Darwin target, is NOT a copy error. ✔MEASURED at test/loadext.test:26-32: the name is chosen from `tcl_platform(platform)` (`unix` on a Mac), and the `tcl_platform(os) eq Darwin` branch three lines down changes only the COMPILER FLAGS (`-dynamiclib`, which is what this leg's sharedLibFlags already say) — never the file name.
build.$librariesComment: ★ THIS LEG ACQUIRES ITS LIBRARIES (D-HARNESS-LIBRARY-ACQUISITION-BUILT-FOR-ONE-LEG-IN-ONE-DRIVER). It used to declare `host-system`, which on any non-Mac means 'hope this box has a Darwin libtcl' — i.e. it never built anywhere but a Mac, in flat contradiction of the harness's own contract that every leg is BUILT everywhere and only RUN is gated. MacPorts publishes unauthenticated-HTTPS binary archives, and the two we need are UNIVERSAL (one download carries both the arm64 and the x86_64 slice, which is why the sibling macho leg names the SAME url + digest and differs only in the slice it takes). ✔MEASURED 2026-08-04: 110/110 required symbols present on BOTH arches — all 102 `Tcl*` the testfixture imports, 0 missing, plus 8/8 zlib — so there is no eager-import hazard [[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]].

libraries.$acquireComment: `universal: true` is not a formality. ✔MEASURED: handed the UNIVERSAL file, DSS refuses it — `error[F_UnsupportedBinaryFormat] readImports: '<path>' is a Mach-O FAT/universal binary (big-endian fat_header magic 0xCAFEBABE or 0xCAFEBABF). v1 supports single-arch Mach-O only — slice the required arch first (e.g. `lipo -thin arm64 in.dylib -output out.dylib`). Anchor D-FF1-MACHO-FAT.` — and handed the thin arm64 slice OF THE SAME FILE it succeeds with rc=0. So slicing is the contract that anchor states, performed here because the harness is the only layer that knows which arch this leg wants (`readImports(path, reporter)` takes no target). ⚠ THE REFUSAL'S SPELLING CHANGED INSIDE THIS CYCLE, and the first draft of this comment quoted the older one: `guessFormat` read the fat magic little-endian, so a real universal binary could never reach the arm above and fell into the unknown-magic catch-all instead — the anchor's own remediation was unreachable. That detection bug was fixed in the same cycle; the quote above is the post-fix message. ★ Slicing would be right even if DSS read fat files: a leg's build input should be a library FOR THAT LEG'S TARGET, not a container that also holds a foreign architecture, or 'which architecture did this leg resolve against?' has no answer from the input.
libraries.$importNameComment: ★★ THE TRAP, AND WHY THE ANSWER IS `@loader_path` AND NOT A SYSTEM PATH. Both archives' LC_ID_DYLIB reads `/opt/local/lib/…` (✔MEASURED: `/opt/local/lib/libtcl8.6.dylib`, `/opt/local/lib/libz.1.dylib`), and DSS records a resolved library's EMBEDDED identity as the LC_LOAD_DYLIB — so linking naively produces a Mach-O that demands MacPorts at that prefix on the target Mac. That is a dyld LOAD failure, not a build error, so nothing on this host would catch it. The obvious fix is to record the system path instead — and this project cannot HONESTLY do that for Tcl: nobody here has measured what a Mac carries at /usr/lib for Tcl 8.6, and this repo's own darwin path installs Tcl through Homebrew, whose current `tcl-tk` is 9.x — so `/usr/lib/libtcl8.6.dylib` would be an unverified claim about someone else's machine, and a wrong one costs a dyld failure. `@loader_path/<name>` is TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION: dyld resolves it against the directory holding the executable, the driver stages the acquired dylib there beside the artefact, and the result assumes NOTHING about the target Mac's prefix layout or Tcl version. ⚠ For zlib a system path WOULD be defensible — this harness has measured that `/usr/lib/libz.1.dylib` resolves out of the dyld shared cache even though it cannot be opened as a file (see build-and-test.sh's darwin branch) — but mixing the two policies inside one artefact buys nothing and makes the rule harder to state. Flipping either back to a system path is a one-line edit HERE, which is the point of declaring it.
libraries.$scriptLibraryComment: ★★ THE DYLIB IS NOT THE WHOLE LIBRARY — D-HARNESS-ACQUIRED-TCL-DYLIB-HAS-NO-SCRIPT-LIBRARY, and this is the declaration that closed it. ✔MEASURED on the operator's Mac at 11e97e0e: this leg's testfixture BUILDS (189 TUs, 0 diagnostics) and runs an individual `.test` file correctly (select1 → 0 errors out of 192), and then the TIER driver aborts INSTANTLY with `Can't find a usable init.tcl in the following directories: /opt/local/lib/tcl8.6 …` raised from `interp create tinterp`. `permutations.test` runs every unit in a fresh SLAVE interpreter and `interp create` re-enters `tclInit`, which needs Tcl's SCRIPT LIBRARY; the MAIN interpreter is already initialised when a directly-named file is sourced, which is why one path passed and the other could not. The acquired dylib bakes in `/opt/local/lib/tcl8.6` — MacPorts' own prefix — and MacPorts is not installed on that Mac; only the dylib was ever downloaded. ⇒ the SAME pinned archive also carries the scripts (✔MEASURED: 225 files, 4 subdirectories, ZERO symlinks under `opt/local/lib/tcl8.6/`, 1,948,034 bytes, `init.tcl` among them), so they are staged from it, pinned by a whole-tree digest, and handed to the drivers as `scriptLibraryDir` for TCL_LIBRARY. ⛔ NOT the host's Homebrew `tcl-tk@8` scripts: that works on ONE Mac, reintroduces exactly the host-dependence this arc exists to end, and pairs an 8.6.18 script library with a MacPorts 8.6.17 binary on nothing but a version-number coincidence.

archives.$embeddedPathsComment: EVERY absolute path this dylib carries, listed ONCE against a PINNED digest so it cannot drift under the declaration — the general guard from the anchor above. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-06: 14 tokens, of which 4 are the loader's own (LC_ID_DYLIB, LC_LOAD_DYLIB ×3) and are excused by the resolver from the file itself. The remaining 10 are here. Exactly ONE is runtime data, and it is the one that cost the corpus.

embeddedPaths.$why: MacPorts' libdir, reported through `tcl_pkgPath`/`tcl_library` for a package search that this fixture never performs — the testfixture loads no Tcl EXTENSION (its own commands are compiled in), and the one directory `tclInit` MUST read is declared runtime-data above.
TCL_PREFIX/bin, reported through `tcl_platform`/`info nameofexecutable` fallbacks. Nothing in the corpus execs out of it.
TCL_INCLUDE_SPEC, a BUILD-time answer baked in for tclConfig.sh consumers. This harness stages its own tcl.h (see the top-level Tcl coherence check) and never reads it.
the manual page directory, from the same tclConfig.sh block. No code path in a Tcl interpreter reads it.
the default PATH element Tcl's `exec` falls back on. A TARGET path that exists on every Mac, not a packager path — nothing to stage.
`exec`'s redirection sink. A device on the target, not data we could ship.
the controlling terminal, opened by `tcl_interactive` prompting. Same category as /dev/null.
the fallback temp directory for `file tempfile` when TMPDIR is unset. A target location, not shipped data.
the HFS+ resource-fork suffix Tcl appends when opening a file's resource fork; a magic SUFFIX, not a directory anyone stages.

archives.$memberComment: The archive ships `libz.1.dylib` as a SYMLINK to `libz.1.3.2.dylib`. The declaration names the link, and the resolver follows it inside the archive and materialises the TARGET's bytes under the `as` name — a symlink is not creatable on Windows without privilege and is not a library DSS can read, so one declaration has to work on every host.

members.$embeddedPathsComment: EMPTY, and measured rather than assumed: the only two absolute paths in this dylib are its own LC_ID_DYLIB and LC_LOAD_DYLIB /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib, both excused by the resolver as the loader's business. zlib reads no data directory — which is exactly why it is the CONTROL for the Tcl declaration above.

build.$sharedLibFormatComment: See macho64-arm64's $sharedLibFormatComment — same story, other slice. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-05 from a Windows host: 17,890 bytes, a single-arch Mach-O 64 x86_64 MH_DYLIB. Not loaded here, for the same reason, and not claimed to have been.
